Themes can either use the bundled dialog or drive window.SearchLite themselves. Explanation Why not Sphinx’s own search? Sphinx ships searchindex.js, but it is tied to searchtools.js and the dedicated search.html page, and there is no supported way to query it from your own UI. searchlite writes plain JSON records instead, so a theme can score and render results however it likes. How ranking works Results are scored with BM25 over the record text, with extra weight for two fields: the record’s own heading, weighted heavily the title of the page it belongs to, weighted lightly These are kept separate because every section of a page shares that page’s title. If both were weighted heavily, searching for a page title would rank its subsections alongside the page itself, often above it. The last word of the query is matched as a prefix as well as exactly, since you are probably still typing it. That way install also finds installation. Results must match every query word that appears in the index, so adding words narrows the results. Words that appear nowhere in the index are ignored. Sphinx ships searchindex.js, but it is tied to searchtools.js and the dedicated search.html page, and there is no supported way to query it from your own UI. searchlite writes plain JSON records instead, so a theme can score and render results however it likes.

Results are scored with BM25 over the record text, with extra weight for two fields: the record’s own heading, weighted heavily the title of the page it belongs to, weighted lightly These are kept separate because every section of a page shares that page’s title. If both were weighted heavily, searching for a page title would rank its subsections alongside the page itself, often above it. The last word of the query is matched as a prefix as well as exactly, since you are probably still typing it. That way install also finds installation. Results must match every query word that appears in the index, so adding words narrows the results. Words that appear nowhere in the index are ignored.

s: Why the dialog takes over the theme’s search box
x: Most themes render a search box that submits to search.html. Left alone, a page would have two different searches, and the dialog would have no visible way to open it. searchlite makes that box read-only and opens the dialog when it is clicked, activated with Enter or Space, or its form is submitted. It does not open on focus, because closing the dialog returns focus to the box, which would open it again.

s: How the dialog picks its colors
x: The dialog reads the page’s background and text colors and copies them onto itself. It watches for changes, so it follows the theme’s light and dark toggle. Most themes switch modes with a class or attribute, which prefers-color-scheme does not detect.

How-to guides Keep the theme’s own search box By default searchlite takes over the theme’s search box so that it opens the dialog. To leave the box wired to Sphinx’s search.html, set: searchlite_adopt_theme_search = False The dialog still opens with / and ⌘K, and from any element with data-searchlite-open. Add a button that opens the dialog Add the data-searchlite-open attribute to any element in your templates: <button type="button" data-searchlite-open>Search</button> Use your own search UI Turn off the bundled dialog so only the engine is shipped: searchlite_ui = False Then query the engine from your own script: const engine = SearchLite.create({ url: SearchLite.indexUrl }); await engine.load(); const { items, terms } = engine.search("query"); for (const item of items) { const snippet = SearchLite.highlight(SearchLite.excerpt(item, terms), terms); // render item.u, item.t, item.s, and snippet } See the JavaScript API for what each call returns. Restyle the dialog Set --searchlite-* custom properties on #searchlite-dialog: #searchlite-dialog { --searchlite-background: #111; --searchlite-foreground: #eee; --searchlite-radius: 0.25rem; } Target the dialog element rather than :root.

Set --searchlite-* custom properties on #searchlite-dialog: #searchlite-dialog { --searchlite-background: #111; --searchlite-foreground: #eee; --searchlite-radius: 0.25rem; } Target the dialog element rather than :root. The dialog copies the page’s colors onto itself at runtime, and those inline values override anything inherited from :root. Setting the background and foreground is usually enough, because the muted, border, and accent colors are mixed from the foreground.

Option Default Description searchlite_index_filename searchlite-index.json Name of the index file written to _static/. searchlite_max_text 1200 Maximum characters of body text kept per record. searchlite_ui True Ship the bundled dialog and its CSS. When False, only the engine is shipped. searchlite_adopt_theme_search True Make the theme’s search box open the dialog. Has no effect when searchlite_ui is False. Index format The index is a JSON array of records. Each page produces one record for the page and one for each section that has an anchor. Key Description u URL relative to the documentation root, with #anchor for sections. t Title of the page. s Section heading. Absent on page records. x Text, truncated to searchlite_max_text. Sections exclude nested sections. engine.load() rewrites u to an absolute URL. JavaScript API The engine defines a global SearchLite object. SearchLite.create({ url }) Returns an engine for the index at url. Nothing is fetched until load() is called. engine.load() Fetches and indexes the records. Returns a promise. sphinx-searchlite Client-side documentation search for any Sphinx theme. It needs no search service, no runtime dependency, and no build step beyond Sphinx itself. Build Status codecov License PyPI Quick start Install the package: pip install sphinx-searchlite Add it to conf.py: extensions = ["sphinx_searchlite"] Build your docs and open any page. Press / or ⌘K (Ctrl+K on Linux and Windows) to open the search dialog. If your theme has its own search box, clicking it opens the same dialog.
